doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: Her music, free jazz and playing
title: Describing her music: melody and beauty
summary: She loves simple melodies and harmonies and sees her work as finding what moves her and creating beauty.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well thank you for that. That was very informative. I want to talk about the music that you play that I’ve been listening to, especially on your website. The tunes, if I had to describe them to people I can’t think of the adjective so I wonder if you have adjectives to describe your music. If someone came up to you at a cocktail party and you said you are a composer and they say, “Well what kind of music do you write?”

I love melodies. I love very simple melodies and I love beautiful harmonies. That’s really — and also as an improviser I love melody. And even when I play free music, which I also love, I tend to want to play melody. That’s always my guiding light. It doesn’t matter what stylistic context even with a big band, I always gravitate towards melody. And I know this is not an adjective and it’s not my elevator speech —
But we have melodious — we could use that.

Yeah melodious for sure. Lyrical. And one thing I realized over the years that is really what I really want to do with music is I want to create beauty and beauty obviously is something different to everybody. There’s no one definition of beauty. But I think one thing that all ideas of beauty have in common is that they move you in some way. And I see it as my job as a musician to really dig deep and to find those things, those melodies, those little motifs, those harmonic movements that move me. And when I sit by the piano I’ll play a chord and then I’ll play something on my horn and I’ll play around until there’s something that grabs me, that just goes like ut — okay — oh wow, okay, oh I like this. And that’s really my job I see as a musician to really zone in to hone into that, to say what is it that makes me move forward in my chair and say ah, what is that. Wow, I like that, I like that. So unearthing what it is that I like that makes me feel good, that feels beautiful to me and that’s what I want to bring forth. That’s what I see as my life’s work in music, to create my definition of beauty in the hopes that it moves other people too.
